title: Cordango Integration Contract
description: What an app may depend on when it uses an external system: entities with typed fields, what can be done to them, how they can be queried and which figures the provider can compute exactly. Provider-independent: a provider says how one API implements it. Never contains a URL, a credential or an API field name.

name.description: The contract's permanent name, dotted: '<namespace>.<name>' ('hubspot.crm' for a provider-specific contract, 'crm.contacts' for a shared one). The dot is required, so a contract can never share a name with an app.

version.description: The MAJOR version. A breaking change is a new major, which is a new contract: apps pin 'name@major'.

entities.description: Entities by key. Keys follow the same rule as app entity keys.

displayField.description: The field a row is known by, as an app entity's displayField.

capabilities.description: What may be done to this entity. A provider that implements the contract must implement every one. 'create', 'update' and 'delete' are accepted by the language and refused by the gate until writes exist.

type.description: An app field type. 'reference' and 'attachment' are not available in contracts yet.

required.description: Every row carries a value. A provider must map it.

readonly.description: Never written by an app, even once writes exist ('id', 'updated_at').

options.description: The values a select or multiselect field may hold.

query.description: How rows of this entity may be asked for. Anything not declared here is refused by the gate in an app, because a filter the provider cannot apply would otherwise be applied to one page of rows and read as the answer.

filter.description: Filterable fields and the operators each allows.

sort.description: Fields the provider can sort by.

aggregate.description: Figures the provider computes exactly, server-side. Absent means not available: an app figure over this entity is then refused rather than counted from one page.
